# `silk/time/text_asn1`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The two time types of ASN.1 in the DER form that X.509 certificates use: UTCTime and
GeneralizedTime.

## When to use

Use this module to read or write the time fields of DER structures such as certificates,
revocation lists, and signed timestamps. `Certificate.notBefore` and `Certificate.notAfter`
already return instants, so a program that only reads certificates does not need it.

## Details

Both functions work on the content bytes of the ASN.1 value, without its tag and length.

- UTCTime is `YYMMDDHHMMSSZ`, 13 bytes. The years `50` to `99` are 1950 to 1999 and the years
  `00` to `49` are 2000 to 2049, as RFC 5280 defines.
- GeneralizedTime is `YYYYMMDDHHMMSSZ`, 15 bytes.

The seconds are required, the zone is always `Z`, and a fraction of a second is not allowed,
which is the profile of RFC 5280. Second `60` is not valid.

## Examples

### Read a UTCTime and write it as a GeneralizedTime

```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.time.instant { Instant }
import silk.time.text { TimeParseError }
import silk.time.text_asn1 { Asn1Time }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  match Asn1Time.parseUtcTime(b"110523203821Z") {
    Result<Instant, TimeParseError>.Success { value } => {
      let mut text: [u8; 15] = [0; 15]
      let length = Asn1Time.writeGeneralizedTime(value, &mut text, 0)
      // `text` is now `20110523203821Z`.
      if length == 15 && text[0] == 50 && text[14] == 90 {
        return 0
      }
      return 1
    }
    Result<Instant, TimeParseError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 2
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="Asn1Time.impl.parseUtcTime"></a>

### Associated function `parseUtcTime`

```silk
pub fn parseUtcTime(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Instant, TimeParseError>
```

Reads an instant from the content of a UTCTime, such as `110523203821Z`.

#### Errors
- `UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if `bytes` is not `YYMMDDHHMMSSZ`.
- `OutOfRange` if the date or the time does not exist, such as month `13` or second `60`.

<a id="Asn1Time.impl.parseGeneralizedTime"></a>

### Associated function `parseGeneralizedTime`

```silk
pub fn parseGeneralizedTime(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Instant, TimeParseError>
```

Reads an instant from the content of a GeneralizedTime, such as `20500101000000Z`.

#### Errors
- `UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if `bytes` is not `YYYYMMDDHHMMSSZ`.
- `OutOfRange` if the date or the time does not exist, such as month `13` or second `60`.

<a id="Asn1Time.impl.writeUtcTime"></a>

### Associated function `writeUtcTime`

```silk
pub fn writeUtcTime(instant: Instant, output: &mut [u8], at: usize) -> usize
```

Writes `instant` as the 13 content bytes of a UTCTime, such as `110523203821Z`, at
`output[at]` and returns `at + 13`.

#### Details

A fraction of a second is dropped. The year of `instant` in UTC must be from 1950 to 2049,
or the function traps. RFC 5280 requires GeneralizedTime for the other years.

<a id="Asn1Time.impl.writeGeneralizedTime"></a>

### Associated function `writeGeneralizedTime`

```silk
pub fn writeGeneralizedTime(instant: Instant, output: &mut [u8], at: usize) -> usize
```

Writes `instant` as the 15 content bytes of a GeneralizedTime, such as `20500101000000Z`,
at `output[at]` and returns `at + 15`.

#### Details

A fraction of a second is dropped. The year of `instant` in UTC must be from 0 to 9999, or
the function traps.
